questions.text: Which physical quantity is the measure of the inertia of a body?
questions.explanation: Mass is the measure of the inertia of a body.

questions.text: The SI unit of force is the ___.
Newton's second law of motion is expressed mathematically as ___.
questions.explanation: The second law gives F = ma.

questions.text: One newton is the force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of ___.
Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of ___.
questions.explanation: The first law is known as the law of inertia.

questions.text: A book on a table stays there until it is pushed or pulled. This illustrates Newton's ___.
questions.explanation: The first law says a body at rest stays at rest unless a force acts on it.

questions.text: Newton's third law states that for every action there is ___.
questions.explanation: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

questions.text: Which of the following is an application of Newton's third law?
questions.explanation: The recoil of a gun is a classic example of action and reaction.

questions.text: Linear momentum is the product of ___.
The SI unit of linear momentum is ___.
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity, so its unit is kg m s⁻¹.

questions.text: Impulse is the product of ___.
The impulse of a force is numerically equal to the ___.
questions.explanation: Ft = mv − mu, the change in momentum.

questions.text: The SI unit of impulse is the ___.
questions.explanation: Impulse = force × time, hence N s.

questions.text: Linear momentum is conserved in a collision provided ___.
options: no external force acts on the system
the colliding bodies have equal masses
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum holds when no external force acts on the system.

questions.text: In an elastic collision, besides momentum, which quantity is conserved?
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision both kinetic energy and momentum are conserved.

questions.text: When two bodies collide and stick together, the collision is said to be ___.
questions.explanation: Sticking together means a perfectly inelastic collision.

questions.text: The coefficient of restitution of a perfectly elastic collision is ___.
questions.explanation: e = 1 for a perfectly elastic collision.

questions.text: The coefficient of restitution of a perfectly inelastic collision is ___.
questions.explanation: e = 0 for a perfectly inelastic collision.

questions.text: Speed is the rate of change of ___ with time.
The unit of speed is ___.
questions.explanation: Speed is distance over time, measured in m s⁻¹.

questions.text: Velocity is the rate of change of ___ with time.
Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction.

questions.text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed is described by magnitude only.

questions.text: Acceleration is the rate of change of ___ with time.
The unit of acceleration is ___.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is velocity per unit time, giving m s⁻².

questions.text: A negative acceleration is called ___.
questions.explanation: Negative acceleration is retardation or deceleration.

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is about ___.
For a body thrown vertically upward, the acceleration due to gravity is taken to be ___.
questions.explanation: For upward motion g is negative.

questions.text: At its maximum height, the velocity of a body thrown vertically upward is ___.
questions.explanation: At maximum height the body is momentarily at rest, v = 0.

questions.text: The first equation of motion under constant acceleration is ___.
questions.explanation: v = u + at is the first equation of motion.

questions.text: The second equation of motion is ___.
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² is the second equation of motion.

questions.text: The third equation of motion is ___.
questions.explanation: v² = u² + 2as is the third equation of motion.

questions.text: A body that covers equal displacements in equal intervals of time moves with ___.
questions.explanation: Equal displacements in equal times mean uniform velocity.

questions.text: If v = u + at with u = 0, a = 2 m/s² and t = 3 s, the value of v is ___.
Using s = ut + ½at² with u = 0, a = 4 m/s² and t = 2 s gives s = ___.
A speed of 50 km/h is approximately equal to ___.
A car moves at 60 m/s and a motorbike ahead of it moves at 95 m/s in the same direction. The velocity of the bike relative to the car is ___.
Work done = force × ___ measured in the direction of the force.
questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement in the direction of the force.

questions.text: The SI unit of work is the ___.
When the displacement is perpendicular to the applied force (θ = 90°), the work done is ___.
The kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with velocity v is ___.
The gravitational potential energy of a mass m at a height h is ___.
The elastic potential energy stored in a stretched spring of force constant k and extension x is ___.
Energy is the ___ of a body.
questions.explanation: Energy is the ability to do work.

questions.text: The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on a body equals its change in ___.
Power is the ___.
questions.explanation: Power = work done per unit time.

questions.text: The SI unit of power is the ___.
One horse power (hp) is equal to ___.
The instantaneous power delivered by a force F to a body moving with velocity v is ___.
When only conservative forces act on a system, the total mechanical energy ___.
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy is conserved when only conservative forces act.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental (base) quantity?
The SI unit of length is the ___.
The SI unit of mass is the ___.
The SI unit of time is the ___.
The SI unit of temperature is the ___.
questions.explanation: Kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature.

questions.text: How many fundamental (base) quantities are there in the SI system?
The dimension of length is written as ___.
The dimension of mass is written as ___.
The dimension of time is written as ___.
The dimension of force is ___.
The dimension of velocity is ___.
The dimension of acceleration is ___.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is velocity per unit time, giving [LT⁻²].

questions.text: The dimension of density is ___.
The dimension of pressure (stress) is ___.
Which of the following quantities is dimensionless?
questions.explanation: Angles and trigonometric functions have no dimension.

questions.text: The magnitude of a unit vector is ___.
By definition, one metre is the distance travelled by light in a vacuum in ___.
questions.explanation: The metre is defined using the distance light travels in 1/299 792 458 s.

questions.text: A vector quantity is fully described by ___.
questions.explanation: Vectors have both magnitude and direction.

questions.text: The dimension of area is ___.
The dimension of volume is ___.
